q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT SUB.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(SUB.EXPERIENCE/SUB.EMPLOYEES,2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM (SELECT P.PROJECT_ID, COUNT(P.EMPLOYEE_ID) AS EMPLOYEES, SUM(E.EXPERIENCE_YEARS) AS EXPERIENCE FROM PROJECT P JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY P.PROJECT_ID) AS SUB GROUP BY SUB.PROJECT_ID

explanation: Q1 calculates the average experience years of employees for each project by dividing the total experience years of all employees in the project by the number of employees in that project. Q2, however, incorrectly calculates the average experience years by dividing the sum of all experience years in the project by the total number of projects, which is incorrect.
counterexample_dsp: A project with two employees, where one employee has 5 years of experience and the other has 10 years of experience. The average experience years for this project should be 7.5 years (total experience / number of employees), but Q2 incorrectly calculates it as 7.5 years (total experience / total number of projects).
